buyer: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board
title: SEL ICB (Bexley) Health & Wellbeing Coaching and Community Health & Wellbeing Workers (CHWWs) with Social Prescribing Service Specification
description: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board (SEL ICB) is seeking to commission a Health & Wellbeing Coaching and Community Health & Wellbeing Workers with Social Prescribing Service for the London Borough of Bexley. This service is for those who live in the London Borough of Bexley or are registered with a Bexley GP practice. Following the publication of the NHS 10 Year Plan, Bexley Place is driving forward with establishing a Neighbourhood Health Service in each of its three neighbourhoods. A fundamental component of a neighbourhood health service is to support residents with the wider determinants of health which have an impact on how they are able to manage their long term conditions. The population in Bexley is diverse, both culturally and economically. The borough is split into 3 Neighbourhoods, these are: • Frognal (Sidcup & Bexley) • Clocktower (Bexleyheath & Welling) • North Bexley (Erith, Thamesmead & Abbey Wood) There are approximately 26,000 people living in Bexley who have 3 or more long term conditions. North Bexley is the most culturally and economically diverse part of the borough, with 15,995 residents living in the lowest 20% deprivation decile - this is 15% of the North Bexley population. In the other parts of the borough, the number of residents living in the lowest 20% deprivation decile is 2,774, which is 2% of that population. People living in the most deprived 20% of Bexley have a shorter life expectancy than those living in the least deprived 20%. For females, the gap is 2.2 years, and for males the gap is 5.2 years. Bexley Place seeks an established provider of voluntary services based in the London Borough of Bexley, with a proven track record in currently delivering social prescribing and peer support services. The provider must be an existing key partner of the integrated neighbourhood teams' development in the London Borough of Bexley. The provider must be able to mobilise within 3 months of the contract award. Due to different funding sources for these roles, the recruitment requirements are as follows: 2 wte Health & Wellbeing Coaches - community outreach - 3 years funding 5 Community Health & Wellbeing Workers - North Bexley (hyperlocal focus on Slade Green / Erith area) There is a likelihood that the provider will be asked to further expand this service with additional resource at a later date, however this will be dependent on further funding becoming available. The Health & Wellbeing Coaching service with Social Prescribing Service aims to: • Identify people who would benefit from Health & Wellbeing Coaching, through primary care, the community or self referral • Undertake proactive vital 5 checks through having a presence at key community engagement events and high footfall locations across the borough, to identify people who may have an undiagnosed CVD condition • To support residents to make positive health and lifestyle changes through motivational coaching and support • To signpost and connect people to organisations that can help them, and follow up on their progress and if they require further support • For residents to make health improvements following changes made as a result of their health and wellbeing coaching - reducing the risk of developing other conditions or exacerbating their existing conditions • For residents to feel more able to self-manage any conditions they have, with a reduced reliance on emergency care Community Health & Wellbeing Workers (CHWWs) are a model of social prescribing and are intended to be a highly local, preventative workforce that works directly with residents and households to improve health, reduce inequalities, and prevent problems escalating into crises.

title: Mental Health Community Step Down Facility
description: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (the Commissioner) is publishing this notice to inform the market of its intention to follow the Most Suitable Provider (MSP) process for the award of a contract for a Mental Health Community Step-Down Facility. The service will provide a 9-bed, community-based step-down facility for adults with severe mental health needs who are ready for discharge from acute inpatient services and require further assessment and support in a non-hospital setting. The Commissioner has a strong preference for providers that can demonstrate their ability to fully mobilise the service within twelve weeks of contract award. Providers should be able to evidence a credible mobilisation plan, including arrangements for premises, workforce, governance, and operational infrastructure necessary to deliver the service from the contract commencement date. Providers who believe they are capable of delivering this service are invited to express their interest within 14 days of publication of this notice. The Commissioner will not begin identifying or assessing potential providers until after this period, in accordance with the Provider Selection Regime The contract duration is 12-months with an optional extension of a further 12-months. The anticipated service commencement date is January 2027. The contract value for the initial 12-month contract is £1,000,000 and the total contract value including the optional 12-month extension period is £2,000,000 excluding VAT This exercise is being carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (SCW) on behalf of the Commissioner.

title: NHSE1108 L&D and RECONNECT Services, Enhanced RECONNECT Services and MH Treatment Requirement Services
description: Liaison and Diversion and Reconnect Services, Enhanced Reconnect Services and Mental Health Treatment Requirement Services for Lancashire and Cumbria North of England Commissioning Support (NECS) is a commissioning support service working for and on behalf of NHS England - North West (the Relevant Authority) who are undertaking a market engagement process via RFI to commission Liaison and Diversion and Reconnect Services, Enhanced Reconnect Services and Mental Health Treatment Requirement Services for Lancashire and Cumbria under the NHS Standard Contract. Liaison and Diversion (L&D) services aim to provide early intervention for vulnerable people as they come to the attention of the criminal justice system. L&D services provide a prompt response to concerns raised by the police, probation service, youth offending teams or court staff, and provide critical information to decision-makers in the justice system, in real time, when it comes to charging and sentencing these vulnerable people. RECONNECT services aim to improve the wellbeing of people leaving prison, reduce inequalities and address health-related drivers of offending behaviours. Enhanced RECONNECT (ER) service builds upon the RECONNECT programme as an enhanced pathway of care. The ER service will work in collaboration with partners, including those from across government to ensure that individuals that have been identified as high risk to the public and have complex health needs that may impact on their risk of reoffending Primary Care Mental Health Treatment Requirement (MHTR) service aims to support individuals whose offending behaviour is linked to mental health needs by providing timely assessment, treatment and therapeutic interventions within Primary Care. The service seeks to offer courts an effective alternative to custodial sentences, address the underlying factors contributing to offending, and reduce the likelihood of reoffending. Proposed Contract Start Date: 01/10/2027 Closing date for submission of the RFI response is by 5pm 4th September 2026

title: Pre-Market Engagement: Automated Teller Machines (ATM) and Currency Services
description: Network Rail (NR) is looking to procure a partner to provide, manage, operate and maintain Automated Teller Machine (ATM) and associated currency services across its managed stations and for Train Operating Company (TOC) stations that may join the arrangement during the contract term. The opportunity will support Network Rail's objective of generating sustainable commercial income from its estate whilst providing a safe, reliable and accessible service for passengers and station users. Network Rail is seeking a Supplier that can deliver a full end-to-end service, including the installation, operation, maintenance, repair, replacement, removal and ongoing management of ATM services, alongside opportunities for technological innovation, enhanced customer experience and foreign currency solutions where appropriate. Network Rail wishes to engage with Suppliers on this opportunity prior to commencing the formal procurement process to better understand market capability, commercial models, revenue generation opportunities, innovation, and best practice. The feedback received will help inform the procurement strategy and final specification requirements (please see Section II.2.4 Description of the Procurement for further information). Network Rail will hold a Supplier Day in London on 21 September 2026 where Suppliers will learn more about this opportunity. Please find details of how to register in the RFI document entitled ‘ATMs -Pre-Market Engagement. This can be found under "view Current Opportunities" on our eSourcing Portal Bravo. In addition, Network Rail will hold 1-2-1 sessions with suppliers who request this in their RFI response. There will be 1 hour slots for the 1-2-1 sessions which will take place in the afternoon of 21 September (after the market engagement presentation/event). Note: Should Network Rail be required to move the Market Engagement event date of 21 September 2026 and the 1-2-1 on the afternoon of the 21 September, Network Rail will inform the supplier who has expressed an interest via the email provided in their RFI response.

title: Market Engagement Event – Brent Parent and Infant Relationship Service (PAIRS)
description: Brent Council intends to commission a comprehensive Parent and Infant Relationship Service (PAIRS) for young families in the Borough hosted within Brent Best Start Family Hubs. The service aligns with national ‘Giving Every Child the Best Start in Life’ guidance released in 2025. The primary aim of the service is to support families with parent-infant relationship concerns and mild to moderate perinatal mental health needs. The provider will be responsible for: • Planning for how the parents and family can support their own wellbeing and that of their infant. • Assessment of the mental health and emotional wellbeing of the mother and infant, with specific attention to the mother-infant relationship and provision of interventions or referral needed to address any problems identified. • Assessment of family functioning and the impact of this on the mother-infant relationship. • Delivery of short-term interventions that are outcome focused. • Ongoing monitoring of maternal mental health as well as infant mental health. • Linking in with peer support service and signposting families. • Building and maintaining collaborative pathways with Brent Children’s Social Care, Health Visiting, CAHMS and safeguarding services • Working with other providers to develop a diversity of service provision which meets the identified needs of diverse communities using the service in Brent. • Working in co-operation with other types of service to ensure that the pathway to support is more coherent and better co-ordinated. A market engagement event has also been scheduled on Wednesday 2nd September 2026 between 1pm - 3pm. If your organisation is interest in attending, please express an interest in the opportunity on the London Tenders Portal. You will then receive a message from the Council requesting further details on how to register for the event.

title: Specialised Paediatric Whole-Body MRI Surveillance for Cancer Predisposing Syndromes
description:
This is an Intended Approach Notice to award contracts using the Most Suitable Provider (MSP) Process for of the provision of Specialised Paediatric whole-body MRI(WBMRI) Surveillance for Cancer Predisposing Syndromes across the following Lots:

Lot 1: London & East of England
Lot 2: Midlands
Lot 3: North East
Lot 4: Yorkshire
Lot 5: North West
Lot 6: South East

Providers must be located in and deliver services from the defined geographical area(s) that they are interested in providing services to.

Inherited cancer predisposition syndromes are genetic conditions that increase the risk of developing one or more types of cancer. This service is for three rare inherited cancer predisposition syndromes; Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD) and rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome (RTPS). Published clinical guidelines for these conditions recommend the use of regular whole-body MRI (WBMRI) with the aim of detecting cancers at an early stage.

The overall aim of WBMRI surveillance for children with cancer predisposing syndromes is to provide WBMRI screening for patients with LFS, CMMRD and RTPS. The provision of expanded capacity within these groups for WBMRI scanning aims to improve clinical care of individuals once an inherited cancer predisposition has been diagnosed.

Providers will:
• Provide, interpret and report WBMRI Scanning for the patient cohort described
•Provide, interpret, and report brain MRI Scanning (the first one with contrast when possible)
•Establish effective pathways with referring and relevant clinical services for referral, undertaking surveillance, timely communication and sharing of imaging results, and onward management where required.
•Have established links and pathways with Regional Genetics Services to support referral, coordination of surveillance, communication of results and continuity of care.
•Demonstrate expertise in the provision, interpretation and reporting of WBMRI, including access to radiologists and multidisciplinary review with experience in the management of patients with cancer predisposition syndromes.
•Facilitate communication with referrers including consultant clinical geneticists
•Have capacity to plan and undertake WBMRI under general anaesthetic if required
•Have information governance processes that permit sharing clinical and imaging data across organisations involved with providing a cancer surveillance service, and collection of clinical outcome and monitoring data;
•Engage positively with associated patient support groups.
•Ensure clear communication with Genetics Services and patients, to support patients to make decisions on where to access screening.
•Work collaboratively with other organisations e.g. within imaging networks, to provide scanning and reporting capacity and expertise to meet the needs of their population including transition between paediatric and adult services.
•Operate appropriate Quality Assessment processes in accordance with CQC requirements and relevant national standards and guidance for MRI safety, quality assurance and reporting.
•Provide facilities will be in line with NHS guidance on Facilities for diagnostic imaging and interventional radiology.
•Support continued educational initiatives for non-genetics health

If you believe your organisation can provide the full set of requirements, please register on the e-Tendering portal at https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome against project reference C462662 to access the MSP documentation and submit your response.

The deadline for submitting completed Expression of Interest Questionnaires and Declarations is 12pm, midday, on Thursday 17 September 2026.

title: Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Service
description: Most Suitable Provider Process: This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention approach notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and Procurement Act Regulations 2023 do not apply to this award. BCP Council, acting on behalf of both BCP Council and Dorset Council, intends to award a contract using the Most Suitable Provider Process for the provision of a fully integrated, open-access Sexual and Reproductive Health Service across the Bournemouth, Christchurch, Poole, and Dorset local authority areas. The service will be awarded as a single contract and will not be divided into lots. The service shall deliver: • Sexual health prevention, testing, diagnosis and treatment services. • Reproductive health and contraception services, including Long Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC). • HIV testing, prevention and Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) services. • Digital and self-managed sexual health pathways, including online information, triage and home testing where clinically appropriate. • Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) support and targeted prevention activity. • Clinical outreach services designed to improve access and reduce health inequalities. • Services for children and young people. • Workforce development, training and public health prevention initiatives. The provider will be expected to deliver a blended model of care comprising: • Face-to-face clinical services, (CQC Registration requirement - Level Good or above) • Telephone consultations. • Digital access routes and online service provision. • Walk-in services where appropriate. • Same-day assessment pathways for urgent clinical need. • Integrated pathways enabling seamless movement between digital, telephone and in-person services. The contract is intended to secure a single provider capable of delivering accessible, high-quality, person-centred services across both council areas, ensuring continuity of care and consistent service standards throughout the contract term. This notice is published to provide transparency regarding the councils' commissioning intentions and does not, in itself, constitute a contract award.

title: ENFOR - Environmental Analysis Services Framework
description: Scottish Government policy is to ensure that materials that cannot be avoided, reused, or recycled are managed in a way that: a.minimises environmental and climate impacts b.encourages management of materials further up the waste hierarchy, and c.minimises broader societal impacts The majority of greenhouse gas emissions in the waste sector come from the decomposition of biodegradable waste in landfills. Landfilling biodegradable waste produces methane, which is 28 times more potent than carbon dioxide. As an important part of delivering Scotland’s net zero ambitions, helping cut harmful emissions and deliver on our climate commitments, the Scottish Government has banned biodegradable municipal waste (BMW) from being sent to landfill. As a consequence of this ban, along with factors such as Scottish Landfill Tax changes to revenue generating schemes such as the Renewables Obligation and sites reaching capacity, many landfills are expected to close over the coming years. In the event of a waste/recycling operator experiencing urgent difficulties that threaten their continued operations, an unplanned closure of a landfill or other waste and/or recycling site, the complete abandonment of a landfill or waste/recycling site, or other urgent and quickly-developing situation that jeopardises the continuity of critical waste or recycling services in Scotland the contracted organisations will be required to attend the site to assess the environmental impacts and potential future risks on both the site and surrounding area.
